name: Vanishing-glass sorter
subtitle: makes good glass invisible to catch contaminants

effects.effect: crushed glass in a liquid lets through only the colour where both bend light equally

effect: crushed glass in a liquid lets through only the colour where both bend light equally
how: One chip of ovenproof glass or ceramic can ruin a furnace-load of new bottles, so much collected glass is landfilled instead. Crushed glass runs through an oil that, in the one colour of light used, bends light exactly as bottle glass does (Christiansen effect): bottle glass turns invisible, while ceramic, stone and heat-proof glass stay bright, and a camera tells air jets to blow them out.
obstacle: Keeping the oil clean and at a steady temperature while tonnes of dirty, labelled glass pass through each hour.
why: Contamination caps glass recycling; making the good glass vanish makes every contaminant obvious.
real: Cullet sorters use IR/optical opacity, XRF, induction heating or Steinert's HR-glass upgrade; index-matched immersion appears only as a bench test for identifying borosilicate, not as a sorting process.
